answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because umber only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any haven approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
